title: On Denying the charge in open court
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：deny　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 deny 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the teacher ① denied the charge in open court in silence, and every pupil in the classroom said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three terms on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the teacher ② denies the charge in open court twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ deny the charge in open court at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ denied the charge in open court before — a line in the notebook for March 1980 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Denying the charge in open court in silence, the teacher said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ruler at the far blackboard, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ deny the family any share at all twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Deny the family any share at all at once and never mention it again.

By 1993 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new pupil from the next classroom ⑧ denies the family any share at all in silence every term without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the blackboard, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ denied the charge in open court again when nobody else would.

⑩ To deny the charge in open court, my mother said in 1998, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the classroom remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the classroom forgets, somebody denies the charge in open court twice over again and somebody must deny the charge in open court in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 否认（一般过去式 denied the charge in open court：1986 年先生头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 否认（一般现在 denies the charge in open court：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 否认（不定式 to deny the charge in open court：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 否认（过去完成时 had denied the charge in open court：1980 年三月的笔记簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 否认（动名词 denying the charge in open court 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 拒绝给予（deny the family any share at all：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去拒绝给予一分也不给那家人）
G. v. 拒绝给予（deny the family any share at all：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 否认（后段两处：新来的学童照例 denies the family any share at all，而母亲又一次 denied the charge in open court）

answers.why: deny 意为“否认”，1986 年先生一言不发地否认在公堂上当众否认指控，那是教室里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 denied。
deny 意为“否认”，自那以后先生来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 denies。
deny 意为“否认”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯否认在公堂上当众否认指控”，此处为不定式 to deny the charge in open court。
deny 意为“否认”，笔记簿里 三月 那行字说明早在 1993 年之前就有人否认过，故用过去完成时 had denied。
deny 意为“否认”，先生说“否认在公堂上当众否认指控这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 denying the charge in open court 作主语。
deny 意为“拒绝给予”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去拒绝给予一分也不给那家人”，should ever 之后用原形 deny the family any share at all。
deny 意为“拒绝给予”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻拒绝给予一分也不给那家人（deny the family any share at all at once），以后再也不要提起。
deny 意为“否认”，新来的学童每个学期都照例拒绝给予一分也不给那家人，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 denies。
deny 意为“否认”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地否认在公堂上当众否认指控，用一般过去式 denied 叙述。
deny 意为“否认”，结尾那句是母亲 1998 年的话：要否认在公堂上当众否认指控，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和教室记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1986 年，先生一言不发地否认在公堂上当众否认指控；教室里每一个学童都说这是头一回。（denied the charge in open court）
多年以后，先生仍来回两遍做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（denies the charge in open court）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯否认在公堂上当众否认指控这件事本身。（to deny the charge in open court）
早在 1980 年就有人否认在公堂上当众否认指控，三月那天笔记簿上的一行字就是证据。（had denied the charge in open court）
先生说过，一言不发地否认在公堂上当众否认指控这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（denying the charge in open court 作主语）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 deny 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1986 the teacher denied the charge in open court in silence, and nobody in the classroom forgot it.
Even now the teacher denies the charge in open court twice over whenever the classroom asks.
Denying the charge in open court in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever deny the family any share at all twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new pupil from the next classroom denies the family any share at all in silence every term, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother denied the charge in open court again, and the classroom remembered that half.
